items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: Milt Hinton and I were in a room, in my house, and we could have played for ten thousand people and it would have been incredible. But it was just he and I.

ctx.x: That is difficult. Because like I say, I am a novice so I really feel I can’t do it. Because I’m slow. It takes me time. Although if they give me a timeline, that helps. Because now I say well this is a chunk of time in order for me to do this. I ask some friends, and I look

at — sometimes I look at some published charts and how much they are charging for the chart itself, and then I say well okay — and I may ask them what kind of budget that you have, and we can discuss it. Because I think it’s just like my performing. Everything’s on sliding scale as far as I’m concerned. And here again I realize they’re asking me now to write something and I would like to be paid as much money as I can possibly get paid. However, I think there is a place and a time where I’ve come now where if…
I’ve been very fortunate to get to know a few of those people, like Milt Hinton. Do you have words to describe what it was like to be around him and that generation of players?

items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Rufus Reed said, “They won‟t let me play, I‟m conducting”, and he conducted us.

ctx.x: The payoff was down at Lincoln Center. They had a 100 bass players out there in Lincoln Center playing happy birthday to me. Little bass players, seven or eight year kids and they all… John Clayton and all these magnificent basses. I tell you it was just great. I really appreciated that. Then the concert at Town Hall, it was really a culmination. We did a piece that I wrote for bass called The Judge Meets The Section and Dick Hyman orchestrated me… for the symphony orchestra for eight basses and we did it with a…

Well you certainly earned it. With a lot of the freelance things that you were discussing earlier, who were some of the people that you recorded with over the years, some that just jump out? I mean it would be impossible to name everybody.
